summary: array-frames typosquat drops and executes obfuscated payload on require()
details: The package is a typosquat impersonating blakeembrey/node-frames (README and author identity replicate the legitimate project; published name is array-frames). Its main entry array-frames.js contains a heavily obfuscated IIFE using a rotating string-array decoder (a0k) that fires on require(). On import, the loader creates ~/.cache/array_modules, writes a synthesized package.json declaring runtime dependencies axios, better-sqlite3, array-machine-id, socket.io-client (plus koffi and an additional dep on Linux), drops an obfuscated JS payload, and spawns process.execPath detached with stdio:'ignore' + unref() to run the payload as a hidden background process. On Windows, the loader resolves wscript.exe via runtime string concatenation ('wscri'+'pt.exe', 'syste'+'m32'), writes main.vbs into ~/.cache, and executes it via wscript or cmd /d /s /c with hidden-window arguments — a LOLBin chain to evade direct Node monitoring. The staged dependency set (socket.io-client for C2, koffi for native FFI, better-sqlite3 for local storage) provisions persistent covert execution infrastructure under the user's home directory. package.json also self-references array-frames@^2.3.5 as its own dependency.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
